reading.body:
In 2002 the Sixth Circuit held that video game and film makers owed no duty for a school shooting allegedly influenced by their content, because the crime was not sufficiently foreseeable and intangible media is not a product for strict liability.

The ruling leaned on the shooter's independent criminal act as a superseding cause. That structure now appears in AI harm litigation: six live cases, including suits against OpenAI and Character Technologies, test whether a system that interacts, personalises and responds in the moment can still be cast as inert media.

The media-violence defense playbook transfers directly to AI harms: no duty to unforeseeable victims of a user's acts, superseding criminal conduct, and content-is-not-a-product. Chatbot harm suits are answered with this case's structure almost paragraph for paragraph. The precedent does not resolve how those live cases will end, only that the seam between inert content and interactive product is now the contested point.

section.name: AI Case Law: The Precedents Behind the Defenses
